title: Expert-first reuse ceiling: does the current routed MMVQ already reuse cross-rank expert overlap?
hypothesis: Strata-style expert-first grouping (decode each distinct expert once per verify window) can only help if the current kernel pays nearly full cost for experts shared across ranks.
inputs: Section 2.31 actual MTP3 captures: 4-token verify windows select 40 experts but only 24.7 (Rust) / 27.1 (JSON) distinct per layer.
runtime: C:\llama-builds\mmvq-rowtail-specialized\fixed (committed row-tail fix, unchanged ggml-cuda.dll); only a diagnostic test-backend-ops.exe is added

fixtures.route0: shuffled: about 40 distinct experts per 4 tokens
fixtures.route1: same ten experts at the same rank for every token: in-CTA reuse
fixtures.route3: same ten experts, rank rotated per token: reuse only across CTAs
fixtures.route4: each 4-token group draws ten of a 32-expert pool: expected 24.85 distinct, close to the captured overlap

statistic: mean of the two run times per case

gates.correctness: new route3/route4 eval cases pass on CUDA0
gates.continue_to_prototype_if: both primary shapes have headroom >= 15% AND T3/T1 >= 1.3
gates.otherwise: stop the expert-first reuse candidate at operator level; record result

limitations: Operator headroom is an upper bound; routed MMVQ is only part of verify time
Unfused operator test; production uses fused gate/up GLU
Linear interpolation by distinct-expert count is a model, not a measured grouped kernel
